images.prompt:
Subject: Two people repair an upturned wooden rowing boat on a pebble beach. An older woman, about 70, sturdy build, short grey hair, weathered face, sleeves rolled up, kneels at the hull and presses a new plank into place with both hands. A young man of about 20, lanky, wearing a knitted cap and a jacket one size too big, crouches beside her and drives a nail into the plank with a small hammer, frowning in concentration. Between them on the stones: an open wooden toolbox, a coil of rope, a tin of nails. Behind them the sea, the end of a wooden jetty and two gulls. Both are absorbed in the work; neither looks at the viewer. Viewpoint and framing are the style's choice.

Constraints: Image format: landscape, 3:2. Keep every person's age, build and imperfections exactly as described; do not beautify, retouch or glamorize anyone. No text, letters or numbers anywhere in the image. No logos, brand names, signatures or watermarks.

images.prompt:
Style: Upper Paleolithic cave-wall painting, France or northern Spain, 40,000–12,000 years ago. Medium: red and yellow ochre, charcoal, swabbed or blown into soft edges, some lines engraved; lumpy cracked limestone, calcite crust, flaked pigment, raking light. Composition: no scenery, ground line, horizon, perspective or light-and-shade modelling; the bare wall is the only space. Interacting figures touch; others sit apart on rock bulges at uneven sizes and angles, overlapping older figures, hand stencils and dot rows. Each is a side-view silhouette: one confident contour, filled flat or blown; people are crude outlines showing age, sex and build; objects are flat side-view outlines. Water becomes wavy finger lines, ground scattered dots, plants single strokes, structures ladder- or roof-shaped signs; distant things are separate figures elsewhere. Lettering, where text is needed: crude finger-traced ochre capitals. Avoid receding landscape, reflections, ink-wash brushwork, woven texture, torches, cartoon cavemen, spirals and stick-figure friezes of later rock-shelter art.

images.prompt:
Style: Tomb wall painting, Thebes, Egypt, about 1400 BC, painted over the painter's red squared grid. Medium: flat Egyptian blue, green, ochres and soot black on dry whitewashed plaster, faint grid lines showing through; red-brown outlines. Composition: everything stands on ruled ground lines, squared to the grid; water blue with black zigzags; ground a plain ochre strip with sparse red dots; bare whitewash above. People: profile head and legs, frontal eye and shoulders; kneeling figures upright, one knee raised; men red-brown, women pale yellow at every age. Lettering, where text is needed: brush-painted letters and numerals in one colour, in ruled boxes. Information, where a diagram, map or chart is shown: steps as successive bands; a chart alone on the wall: plain flat-colour bars on the bottom ground line, heights read off the grid in exact proportion, numeral just above each; maps as top-view plans. Avoid gold, deities and hieroglyphs.

Information, where a diagram, map or chart is shown: scenes in stacked medallions read from the bottom up. images.prompt:
Style: A New Vision photograph, avant-garde camera work from the Bauhaus and Moscow Constructivism around 1925-1932, as a black-and-white gelatin silver print. Medium: handheld 35 mm camera, 50 mm lens, black-and-white roll film, hard direct sunlight; deep shadows, bright highlights, few midtones; visible grain. Composition: camera pointed steeply down from above or up from the ground, never at eye level; main lines run diagonally across the frame; figures and objects cut off hard by frame edges; near forms large and foreshortened; long cast shadows and repeated slats, steps or railings form parallel bands; wide plain areas of ground or sky. Lettering, where text is needed: painted or stencilled sans-serif capitals on objects in the scene, caught at the same steep angle; otherwise none. Avoid eye-level centred framing, a merely tilted horizon, shallow-focus bokeh, smooth digital monochrome, warm or sepia tone, soft pictorialist haze, sober frontal New Objectivity records and photomontage.

In the middle ground a single-arch stone footbridge crosses it; next to the bridge stands a cluster of five or six small houses and one modest chapel, none of them a recognizable real building. Terraced fields climb the left slope, a dense patch of forest covers the right slope. In the foreground a single large, old tree leans slightly toward the river, with a wooden bench beneath it. Far behind, a jagged mountain ridge closes the valley. A small flock of birds crosses above the river; at most one tiny figure stands on the bridge. Season, weather and time of day are left to the style.

Composition: one visual metaphor carries the sheet: two things merge or turn into each other as one large, flat, cropped shape on a plain painted ground; no scene, no horizon, no depth; wide empty colour field; witty, slightly unsettling. Lettering, where text is needed: brush-painted irregular capitals or loose script written into or around the shape; title large, other lines small. Information, where a diagram, map or chart is shown: one painted sign per fact, hand-lettered numbers, no grid. Avoid glossy digital surrealism, smooth gradients, vector shapes, typeset fonts, a sun disc over the horizon, centred posing figures, polished surrealist oil painting and socialist-realist propaganda.
parts.motif: Subject: Conceptual editorial illustration for a magazine article about repairing things instead of replacing them. images.prompt:

Everything else is cold: wood, tools, loose cloth, cold food and ground one flat violet, still readable as dim shapes; metal, water and sky almost black. Warm prints stay where hands rested. Colour changes only in broad soft gradients, edges smeared and rounded; palette black, violet, red, orange, white. Composition: close and plain, subjects cut by the frame edges, thin centre crosshair, vertical colour scale at right. Lettering, where text is needed: tiny white blocky corner readouts. Avoid highlights, glowing outlines, night-vision green, logos.

Avoid gold, deities and hieroglyphs.

images.prompt:
Style: A hand-coated cyanotype, the iron-based sun print of 19th-century England. Medium: Prussian blue and bare paper white only; watercolour paper hand-brushed with sensitiser, leaving ragged stroke edges, drips and thin patches; soft detail, blocked shadows. Composition: the blue field sits inside a wide unprinted margin. People and scenes print from a glass negative: still, eye level, plainly framed. Anything otherwise drawn becomes a photogram: cut paper, tissue and lace laid flat, no perspective, soft-edged white and pale-blue silhouettes. Lettering, where text is needed: white on blue, inked on tracing paper in a careful 19th-century hand or stencil capitals. Information, where a diagram, map or chart is shown: unboxed cut-paper shapes laid out like album specimens, a handwritten label beneath each; quantities as paper strips cut to length; lines in thin white ink. Avoid blue-filtered digital photos, glossy cyan, digital gradients, boxed tile grids and the gridded engineering blueprint.
